hints: Look closely at photomicrograph Y. Notice the very long, thin cells stacked end to end with flat cross walls, but with no thick dark walls.
Recall how phloem sieve tube elements look in longitudinal section compared to lignified xylem vessels, and where phloem sits inside a stem vascular bundle.
walkthrough:
**Read Photomicrograph Y**

Look at Y first. You see long, narrow, living cells placed end to end in vertical files. The cross walls are still present as dark horizontal lines. These are sieve plates.

There is no thick lignified wall and no open hollow tube, so this is not xylem.

**Recall Stem Anatomy in TS**

In a typical young stem in transverse section, each vascular bundle has xylem toward the inside and phloem toward the outside. Phloem is made of very small, thin-walled cells with no lignin.

Sieve tube elements and companion cells look tiny and crowded in TS, but long with sieve plates in LS.

**Match Y Back to X**

Label C points to the cluster of very small, thin-walled cells in the centre of the vascular bundle. That is the phloem tissue.

That matches perfectly with the sieve tubes seen in longitudinal section in Y, so the answer is C.

options.A: A points to the epidermis, a single outer layer of small protective cells, not long sieve tubes.
options.B: B points to cortex collenchyma, large rounded cells with unevenly thickened walls for support, not phloem.
options.C: C points to phloem in the vascular bundle. Its sieve tube elements appear small in TS but long with sieve plates in LS as shown in Y.
options.D: D points to large thin-walled parenchyma cells of the pith, for storage, not long conducting cells.
